title: Quarterly playbook & deliverables: Reserved pools scaling and burst strategy
creator: Rahul Patel
body:
Objective: Create a repeatable quarterly playbook and implementation roadmap for Reserved Pools scaling and burst behavior that reduces p99 latency regressions during peak events, improves cost predictability for customers on Dedicated, and provides clear runbooks for on-call and sales engineering. This ticket captures scope for the quarter: goals, measurable success criteria, milestones, cross-functional owners, trade-offs, and communications plan.

Background: Over the past two quarters we observed two classes of production issues: (1) transient capacity shortages when multiple customers simultaneously burst above reservation, and (2) suboptimal autoscale decisions that increased cost for reserved customers without latency benefit. We have prototype RBAC gating for burst tiers and a kernel-level batching improvement in ENG-4728; this work coordinates product requirements with engineering delivery and go-to-market.

Goals (OKRs):
- Objective: Improve reserved-pool stability and economics
  - KR1: Reduce incidents caused by reserved-pool saturation by 60% vs baseline (baseline = Q3 incident count)
  - KR2: Reduce median cost-per-1M-tokens delivered from reserved pools during mixed-workload windows by 12%
  - KR3: Ship a customer-facing guidance doc and a Console feature flag for burst controls with adoption by at least 3 enterprise customers in pilot

Scope for the quarter:
- Product: define burst tier semantics (soft vs hard limits), quota mapping to billing classes, UI flows for enabling/disabling burst and notifications.
- Eng: implement prioritized autoscale policy engine for Reserved pools (policy language + simulation harness), quota enforcement fallback path, and SLO-aware preemption rules.
- Console: add per-pool dashboard tile showing reserved vs burst consumption, forecasted burn rate, and suggested commit adjustments.
- Docs/SE: customer-facing playbook for capacity planning, cost tradeoffs, and escalation steps.

Success criteria (release gated):
- Autoscale policy engine reaches 95% unit test coverage and passes performance benchmarks at 2x production QPS in staging.
- Console dashboard shows <5% query overhead and correct reconciliation for at least three internal test customers.
- Pilot customers report no capacity-related errors during a 4-week stress window and accept the burst controls in writing.

Milestones & timeline:
- Week 1-2: Align API contract (product + eng) and finalize policy primitives; PRD linked (https://confluence.redwood.ai/ReservedPools-Playbook).
- Week 3-6: Engineering sprint: policy engine MVP + unit tests; Console dashboard prototype.
- Week 7-9: Integration testing, performance validation, chaos testing with simulated multi-tenant bursts.
- Week 10-12: Pilot with 2-3 customers, iterate on UI/flights, finalize docs and runbook.
- Week 12-13: Rollout plan and go/no-go review with GTM and security.

Trade-offs considered:
- Hard caps reduce customer surprise but may increase immediate errors; soft caps preserve availability at cost of higher tail latency for others. We recommend a hybrid: soft cap with SLO-aware preemption and explicit billing notifications.
- Prioritizing cost reduction (aggressive quantization/packing) can increase infra risk; schedule those as phased opt-in recommendations rather than default.

Open questions:
- Billing model for burst: bill on peak sustained usage vs consumed tokens during burst window? (need finance input)
- Acceptable preemption thresholds for enterprise customers with critical latency SLOs (legal/security constraints).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Policy engine misconfiguration leads to cross-tenant impact. Mitigation: feature-flag rollout, circuit-breaker, and admin override with audit log.
- Risk: Console telemetry lag prevents accurate forecasting. Mitigation: fall back to short-window sampling and conservative recommendations.

Communications & rollout:
- Internal: Weekly sync with Eng (runtime/autoscale), Console, Docs, and Sales Engineering; status updates posted to #reserved-capacity.
- External: Publish pilot invite email to top Reserved customers; provide migration guide and cost calculator template.

Artifacts and links:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ReservedPools-Playbook
- Simulation harness/benchmarks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reserved-pools-sim
- Draft Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/console-mockups/reserved-pools
- Related tickets: ENG-4728 (kernel batching), ENG-5019 (quota enforcement), PM-12847 (forecasting improvements)

Next steps (owner: Monica):
1) Run alignment meeting with runtime/infra and finance to finalize billing treatment (by 2025-11-10).
2) Triage open API questions, create ENG subtasks for policy primitives.
3) Schedule pilot customers and prepare test plans.
